Establishment of the Muslim League: 1906

After the success of the Simla Deputation, the Muslim leaders felt the need to establish a political party of their own, so that on important occasions this party could present the Muslims’ point of view before the British government and protect their interests. Sir Salimullah Khan proposed that after the regular session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference to be held in Dhaka in December 1906, an informal session of Muslim leaders should be held in which a political party named the All India Muslim Confederacy would be established.

In December 1906 the session of the Muhammadan Educational Conference was held in Dhaka. Since it was a non-political institution — Sir Syed Ahmad Khan had strictly forbidden bringing political matters under discussion in its sessions — therefore, to bring the proposed Muslim political party into being, an informal session was held immediately after the regular session of the conference, presided over by Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk. In his presidential address he said that it was necessary for the Muslims to establish a separate political party for the protection of their political rights. After the presidential address a resolution was presented in the session under which a Muslim political party named the All India Muslim League was brought into being, whose basic aims were as follows:

1. To promote feelings of loyalty to the British rulers among the Muslims and to remove misunderstandings about the government’s measures and intentions among them.

2. To protect the political and other rights of the Muslims and to present their wishes and demands before the government in a proper manner.

3. Without harming the above aims, to prevent negative feelings against other communities from growing among the Muslims.

The constitution of the Muslim League was framed in 1908. Sir Sultan Muhammad Agha Khan (III) was appointed president of the Muslim League, and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk joint secretaries. Through the efforts of the Muslim leaders the Muslim League within a short time emerged as the representative political party of the Muslims, and after the Quaid-e-Azam joined the Muslim League its popularity increased even further.

In the early period the Muslim League urged the Muslims to be loyal to and cooperate with the British government, but when in 1911 the British government, contrary to the wishes of the Muslims, announced the annulment of the partition of Bengal, the Muslim League in 1913 also amended its aims and added the following points to its aims:

1. Efforts shall be made to attain such a system of self-government as is suitable for India.

2. To achieve this aim, cordial relations, cooperation and joint action with the other communities and political organisations of India shall be promoted.

After this change in the aims of the Muslim League, a short period of cooperation began between the Congress and the Muslim League, whose result emerged in the form of the Lucknow Pact in 1916.

Although all past efforts for Hindu–Muslim unity had failed, in 1916 an agreement was made between the Congress and the Muslim League, as a result of which a temporary but important period of Hindu–Muslim unity continued for the next five years. This agreement was named the Lucknow Pact, and the Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah played an important role in making it possible. This agreement was in fact based on agreed proposals presented by both parties regarding the future constitutional structure of India.

Through the Lucknow Pact the Muslims achieved a great success at that time when the Congress, in this agreement, unconditionally accepted the principle of separate electorates (Right of Separate Electorates) for the Muslims. Besides this, in the Muslim-minority provinces the Muslims were given more seats than the proportion of their population, i.e. weightage. Hindu–Muslim unity continued until the end of the Khilafat Movement.

میثاقِ لکھنؤ سے مسلمانوں کو اُس وقت ایک بڑی کامیابی حاصل ہوئی جب کانگریس نے اس معاہدے میں مسلمانوں کے لیے جداگانہ طرزِ انتخاب کا اُصول (Right of Separate Electorates) بغیر کسی شرط کے تسلیم کر لیا۔ اس کے علاوہ مسلم اقلیتی صوبوں میں مسلمانوں کو اُن کی آبادی کے تناسب سے زیادہ نشستیں یعنی (Weightage) دی گئی۔ ہندو مسلم اتحاد تحریکِ خلافت کے اختتام تک جاری رہا۔
